readerQuestion: How do I use one NFC tag to start a Home Assistant routine from Android or iPhone, and what should I check when scanning only opens a prompt?
directAnswer: Write a shared Home Assistant tag through the Companion app, attach a Tag trigger, and verify it with a persistent on-screen notification before adding one lamp. Both phones need working server access and applicable approvals. A tag is a convenience control, not an access credential.
originalContribution: The worked example in #worked-example starts with a message-only automation and then adds a reading lamp with an explicit on action. #acceptance supplies five observable pass/fail outcomes for two phones, repeated scans, declined approvals and ordinary lamp controls. #troubleshooting isolates reading, OS handoff, app approval, server receipt, automation and lamp control.
limitations: Documentation research and local publishing/browser checks only. No NFC tags, Android phones, iPhones, locks or Home Assistant installation were physically tested. The YAML is a documented configuration example, not a hardware benchmark. Exact phone lock-screen behavior, prompts, app labels and light integration capabilities vary. The generated cover is clearly disclosed as an illustration.

claimChecks.claim: Home Assistant tags use a shared tag URL; the Companion app sends the identifier to the configured server. Read-only media cannot be written as a new tag.
The Tags integration documents phone writing, tag last-scan information, event fields and background NFC reading on iPhone XS/XR and iPhone 11 or later.
Home Assistant 2026.9 moved Tags under Settings > Connectivity; older Settings > Tags instructions need qualification.
Android tag-forwarding protection was fixed in Companion 2026.5.3. The approval UI supports Allow Once/Always and revoking stored approvals; dismissing it forwards nothing.

iOS tag-forwarding protection was fixed in Companion 2026.5.0; unknown tags require approval, with allowed-tag management. A link can arrive from another app, so matching tag/scanner data is not proof of physical presence.
Tag triggers match tag_id and optionally scanner device_id; Events can listen for tag_scanned. This trigger filter is not represented as server authorization.
persistent_notification.create displays a message in Home Assistant's frontend. Reusing notification_id replaces the existing notification; it is not a mobile push notification.
Light turn_on and toggle are separate actions. The example selects turn_on to keep repeated accepted scans from intentionally reversing the lamp state.
A lamp exposed as a switch requires the switch action domain rather than assuming it is a light entity.
Run actions bypasses triggers and top-level conditions, so physical scanning and Traces are required to verify the end-to-end tag path.
Apple Shortcuts NFC triggers register a physical tag identifier and ignore other tag contents, unlike dispatching the Home Assistant tag URL.
The current Companion Perform action App Intent requires iOS 17 or later, uses an explicitly selected server and JSON action data; older Call Service actions are deprecated.
